subject: Interzone attack runbook, tenant boundary evidence & follow-ups
body:
From: Alice Carver <alice.carver@orestone.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: security@orestone.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orestone RFI: interzone egress chains and tenant boundary scenarios

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor review we need a short, scenario-driven runbook that explains: 1) how traffic can flow between zones (control plane, inference zone, tenant enclaves), 2) the expected observable telemetry for each step, and 3) evidence artifacts you can provide for auditors (diagrams, packet capture guidance, config exports).

We're especially focused on multi-tenant blast-radius scenarios where an attacker escalates from a compromised inference container to cross-tenant data access via an interzone egress chain. Can you provide a concise attack-path runbook plus any isolation evidence you can share? A PDF network diagram is fine.

Target deadline: COB next Friday (2028-03-11). Let me know if you need a call.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Carver
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Orestone Financial
security@orestone.com

---

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alice Carver <alice.carver@orestone.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orestone RFI: interzone egress chains and tenant boundary scenarios

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short runbook and the current network diagram (network_diagram_v3.pdf). Summary below; full details and artifacts in the attachment and the isolation evidence bundle.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Attack vector we model: compromised inference process -> privilege escalation to host-side sidecar -> lateral egress via misconfigured service endpoint -> cross-tenant request to a shared model shard.
- Mitigations in place: strict namespace-level network policies, per-tenant mTLS with mutual-auth, control-plane ACLs, egress route whitelists, automatic KV-cache isolation, and per-request tenant provenance headers that are validated at service boundaries.
- Observable indicators: anomalous inter-host TLS session patterns, unusual KV cache invalidations, cross-tenant header values in request traces, and control-plane audit entries showing nonstandard model pinning.

What we included in the attachments:
- network_diagram_v3.pdf: annotated zones (control, inference, tenant-enclave) and allowed egress lanes.
- isolation_evidence_bundle.tar.gz: sanitized config exports, sample audit logs (6 hours), and per-route ACL snapshots.

Next steps: if Orestone wants, Rishi can provide a short run-through of the runbook and point to exact log fields you should pull during an audit.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

Attachment stubs:
- network_diagram_v3.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)
- isolation_evidence_bundle.tar.gz (logs + configs, 24MB)

---

On Wed, 7 Mar 2028 at 08:05 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jasmine / Alice,
>
> Adding a few technical clarifications to the runbook so it's actionable for your ops/audit teams:
>
> 1) Sidecar escape surface: our sidecar runs a read-only socket for model request intake; host-bind mounts are not used for tenant data. If a sidecar process is compromised, it cannot write to host namespaces. Evidence: container runtime mount table (included in isolation bundle).
>
> 2) Control-plane auth chain: we require signed JWTs with tenant-scoped claims for every model invocation. The runbook references the header x-rw-tenant-provenance and the policy checks that reject requests with missing or mismatched claims. Audit artifact: example policy decision log (isolation_evidence_bundle/policy_decision.log).
>
> 3) Interzone egress choke points: we maintain dedicated egress proxies per-availability zone with enforced allowlists. They perform TLS termination and validate mutual TLS to destination clusters; they also tag flows with zone and tenant IDs for tracing.
>
> 4) Observable telemetry fields: trace.span.attributes includes 'tenant.id', 'zone.id', and 'egress.proxy.id'. Our recommendation for auditors is to query traces where span.duration > 2000ms and tenant.id mismatches storage.owner_id.
>
> Happy to join a call to walk devops through the logs.
>
> -Rishi
> Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orestone RFI: interzone egress chains and tenant boundary scenarios

Alice —

Quick operational note for the timeline: we produced a sanitized evidence set in the bundle that aligns with your auditor checklist (we removed customer-identifying tokens and IPs). If your auditors want raw artifacts we can provide a scoped access window to a secure share under an NDA addendum; that usually takes 24–48 hours to arrange.

Also flagging two optional controls you might ask us to enable during a security assessment window:
- strict-mode egress filtering (block-list everything except explicit allowlist entries)
- temporal model pinning (prevent new model shard fetches for the duration of the assessment)

If Orestone wants both controls on for the audit window, we should finalize the start/end times so our ops team can schedule the changes.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Team —

Received everything, thanks. The runbook reads well and the artifacts look sufficient for initial attestation. Two quick asks before we close the RFI:

1) Can you confirm the exact log query to pull the policy decision entries you referenced? We want a one-liner our auditors can use.
2) We'd like to trial strict-mode egress filtering for a 6-hour window next Thursday 2028-03-18 02:00–08:00 UTC. Can you confirm you can schedule this and whether there are expected service impacts?

If we get both answers we can mark the RFI as answered and proceed to scheduling an audit call.

Best,
Alice
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Orestone Financial
